summary: EU leaders discussed rising energy prices and carbon market reform at the Brussels summit on 15-16 October, focusing on industrial competitiveness amid high energy costs.

title: PetroChina Tarim 1.2 million t/y ethylene and green low-carbon demonstration project starts commercial operation
titleZh: 中国石油塔里木120万吨/年乙烯及配套绿色低碳示范工程投入商业运营
summary: PetroChina announced that its Tarim 1.2 million t/y ethylene and green low-carbon demonstration project in Xinjiang has started commercial operation, combining green power, CO2 capture, blue hydrogen and blue ammonia.
summaryZh: 10月15日，中国石油宣布新疆塔里木120万吨/年乙烯及配套绿色低碳示范工程全面投入商业运营。项目将绿色电力、二氧化碳捕集、蓝氢、蓝氨及化工生产相结合，采用低浓度二氧化碳捕集技术，并计划每年消纳超过10亿千瓦时光伏电力。
sourceName: 中国石油
bodyZh: 10月15日，中国石油宣布新疆塔里木120万吨/年乙烯及配套绿色低碳示范工程全面投入商业运营。项目将绿色电力、二氧化碳捕集、蓝氢、蓝氨及化工生产相结合，采用低浓度二氧化碳捕集技术，并计划每年消纳超过10亿千瓦时光伏电力。该工程被视为传统石化基地向绿色低碳转型的示范项目，涉及绿电消纳、碳捕集与化工产业链耦合等环节。

bodyZh: 10月14日，全国首批跨境绿色电力证书集中交易在广州达成，成交绿证约10万张，对应近1亿千瓦时可再生能源电量。交易采用“双代理”模式，由内地绿电绿证服务机构与香港交易所平台分别服务两地市场主体，通过广州电力交易中心完成交易。香港采购方涵盖金融、房地产、教育及公共服务机构，此次交易被视为跨境绿证流通与香港绿色金融基础设施衔接的试点。

body: Government/ Sustainable Finance Mark Segal September 29, 2026 Italy’s Ministry of Economy and Finance announced the completion of a new green bond offering, raising €8 billion to finance projects with a positive environmental impacts, in areas including renewable energy, energy efficiency and clean transport. The ministry reported strong demand for the new 12-year green bond, with the offering more than 13x oversubscribed, and an order book exceeding €110 billion. The offering received orders from more than 330 investors across 35 countries, with approximately 75% from foreign investors. ESG investors accounted for approximately 80% of the placement, the ministry added. The offering follows the release in late 2025 of Italy’s new Green Bond Framework, which included updated criteria for identifying and reporting environmentally sustainable expenditures, and aimed to criteria for identifying and reporting environmentally sustainable expenditures. The green bond framework outlines 6 categories for eligible use of proceeds, including Renewable energy, Energy efficiency, Clean transport, Measures for climate and environmental resilience, Protection of the environment, water and biological diversity, and Environmental research. The ministry said that funds from the new offering will be allocated across all six categories, while the main components will target energy efficiency interventions for buildings and the transport category. Lead managers on the issuance included, Barclays, BNP Paribas, Deutsche Bank, Intesa Sanpaolo, JP Morgan and Société Générale.

body: Mark Segal September 29, 2026 The Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) announced plans to expand its sector standards with the development of a new standard designed to enable food and beverage companies to report on relevant impacts in their industries and value chains. The new planned food and beverage reporting standard will be the first to pilot GRI’s new streamlined approach to Sector Standards development, designed to significantly reduce the time needed for development. GRI Sustainability Reporting Standards are one of the most commonly accepted global standards for sustainability reporting by companies, developed to enable consistent reporting across companies and industries, providing clearer communication regarding sustainability matters to a broad range of stakeholders, including investors. The GRI’s standards are developed by the Global Sustainability Standards Board (GSSB). GRI sector standards aim to help identify sectors’ most significant impacts, and to reflect stakeholder expectations for sustainability reporting. The GRI published its first sector standard in 2021 covering the oil and gas sector, followed by standards for sectors including coal, agriculture, aquaculture and fishing, mining, and textiles and apparel. Sectors selected for standard development are prioritized based on the seriousness and the likelihood of their impacts, with consideration also given to the overall size of the sector, their distribution around the world, and the number of organizations that are in a position to use the GRI Standards. On its project page, GRI noted that food and beverage industries are responsible for around one third of global emissions, have a direct impact on people’s health, and present safety risks for their workers. The new standard will cover food processing, manufacturing of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages, and tobacco products, and will consider impacts across companies’ own operations and value chains, including connections with agriculture, aquaculture, and fishing. GRI’s new streamlined sector standard development approach is designed to enable faster delivery of industry-specific impact reporting guidance.
bodyZh: 马克·西格尔 (Mark Segal) 2026 年 9 月 29 日 全球报告倡议组织 (GRI) 宣布计划扩大其行业标准，制定一项新标准，旨在使食品和饮料公司能够报告其行业和价值链的相关影响。新计划的食品和饮料报告标准将是第一个试点 GRI 新的简化行业标准制定方法的标准，旨在显着减少制定所需的时间。 GRI 可持续发展报告标准是公司最普遍接受的可持续发展报告全球标准之一，旨在实现跨公司和行业的一致报告，为包括投资者在内的广泛利益相关者提供有关可持续发展问题的更清晰的沟通。 GRI 的标准由全球可持续发展标准委员会 (GSSB) 制定。 GRI 行业标准旨在帮助确定行业最重大的影响，并反映利益相关者对可持续发展报告的期望。 GRI 于 2021 年发布了涵盖石油和天然气行业的首个行业标准，随后又发布了煤炭、农业、水产养殖和渔业、采矿以及纺织服装等行业的标准。选择用于标准制定的行业是根据其影响的严重性和可能性来确定优先顺序的，同时还考虑该行业的总体规模、其在世界各地的分布以及有能力使用 GRI 标准的组织数量。 GRI 在其项目页面上指出，食品和饮料行业排放量约占全球排放量的三分之一，对人们的健康有直接影响，并给工人带来安全风险。新标准将涵盖食品加工、酒精和非酒精饮料的制造以及烟草产品，并将考虑对公司自身运营和价值链的影响，包括与农业、水产养殖和渔业的联系。 GRI 全新简化的行业标准制定方法旨在更快地交付针对特定行业的影响报告指南。

body: Kenny Fisher September 29, 2026 Netherlands-based insurance group Achmea’s investment unit, Achmea Investment Management, and asset manager ILX Management announced a partnership aimed at providing an emerging markets debt impact vehicle for Dutch pension funds. Under the agreement, Achmea will contribute its experience in supporting clients address issues including climate change, biodiversity restoration, health, and equal opportunities, while ILX will provide its expertise in private debt investments in EMDEs and its relationships with development finance institutions. Maureen Schlejen, Chair of the Executive Board of Achmea IM, said: “With ILX, we have found a partner with unique expertise, experience, networks, and access to investment opportunities in emerging markets.

body: Energy Transition/ Private Equity & Venture Capital Kenny Fisher September 29, 2026 Fuel cell technology startup Reverion announced today that it has raised $175 in a Series B funding round, with proceeds aimed at significantly scaling up production of its power plants, capable of generating carbon negative energy to power industrial sites and data centers. Founded in 2022 as a spin-off from the Technical University of Munich, Germany-based Reverion develops power plants based on solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) technology that can generate electricity from biogas, natural gas or hydrogen. The systems also capture CO2 in the fuel stream for re-use or permanent storage. According to Reverion,when operated using biogas and combined with permanent storage of the captured biogenic CO2, the process can generate negative emissions. The company said that its solution is also reversible, enabling its plants to switch from electricity generation to electrolysis and use surplus electricity to produce hydrogen or methane for storage, enabling the system to generate power when renewable electricity supply is insufficient and to convert excess power into storable gases when there is excess renewable electricity on the grid. According to Reverion, its solid oxide fuel cell power plant technology converts biogas, natural gas, or hydrogen into electricity on demand at a world-record electrical efficiency of 74.2% – nearly double that of conventional generators. The company said that the new the majority of the new capital will be used for investment into a new megafactory in Germany, scaling its manufacturing capacity tenfold to 250 MW. Reverion noted that seven of its power plants are already in regular operation at customer sites, and that it is seeing demand outside of Germany, with its first international projects scheduled for delivery this year. Stephan Herrmann, CEO and co-founder of Reverion, said: “Solar and wind give us clean energy, but only when the weather cooperates. What the world needs is clean power on tap. By closing this Series B, we are laying the foundation for industrial mass production.

body: Mark Segal September 29, 2026 The International Organization for Standardization’s (ISO) long-awaited proposed net zero standard, ISO 14040, failed to pass a vote by member organizations required to advance to become a final standard in its current form, ESG Today has confirmed, after receiving record feedback throughout its 12-week consultation period. ISO said that the new proposed standard, designed to support companies in developing credible and comprehensive net zero transition plans, received nearly 5,000 comments. While the organization does not disclose the votes of individual member bodies or the reasons behind their positions, media reports citing sources familiar with the process, indicated that the opposition to the draft came from fossil fuel-producing countries. In an email communication to ESG Today, an ISO spokesperson confirmed that “ISO/DIS 14060 did not receive the level of approval required to advance in its current form.” The draft standard, released following a 2-year development process, was designed to provide globally consistent guidance for companies and other organizations navigating the transition to net zero, including setting out requirements for demonstrating that their strategy, targets and actions are compatible with reaching net zero, and that they are making credible and verifiable progress towards contributing to global net zero, in line with the Paris Agreement. Key requirements for alignment with the proposed standard included setting interim and long-term emissions reduction targets, and the publication of a transition plan within two years of setting a target, covering aspects including timelines, integration of strategy into the business model, and measurement and reporting on progress, as well as requirements for validation and verification. ISO released its draft net zero standard in June 2026. Following the typical process for a new proposed standard, ISO initiated a 12-week public consultation period through its national members in more than 170 countries.
bodyZh: 马克·西格尔 (Mark Segal) 2026 年 9 月 29 日 ESG Today 在 12 周的咨询期内收到创纪录的反馈后证实，国际标准化组织 (ISO) 期待已久的拟议净零标准 ISO 14040 未能通过成员组织的投票，而该标准需要推进成为当前形式的最终标准。 ISO 表示，新提议的标准旨在支持企业制定可靠且全面的净零转型计划，已收到近 5,000 条评论。虽然该组织没有透露各个成员机构的投票情况或其立场背后的原因，但媒体报道援引熟悉该过程的消息人士的话说，对该草案的反对来自化石燃料生产国。在给 ESG Today 的一封电子邮件中，ISO 发言人确认“ISO/DIS 14060 没有获得以当前形式推进所需的批准级别”。该标准草案经过两年的制定过程后发布，旨在为公司和其他组织向净零过渡提供全球一致的指导，包括提出要求，证明其战略、目标和行动与实现净零相一致，并且根据《巴黎协定》，在为全球净零做出贡献方面正在取得可信和可验证的进展。与拟议标准保持一致的关键要求包括设定中期和长期减排目标，并在设定目标后两年内公布过渡计划，涵盖时间表、战略与业务模式的整合、进展的衡量和报告以及验证和核查的要求等方面。 ISO 于 2026 年 6 月发布了净零标准草案。按照新拟议标准的典型流程，ISO 通过 170 多个国家的国家成员启动了为期 12 周的公众咨询期。

body: Mark Segal September 29, 2026 Sustainability-linked executive pay became a phenomenon in the early 2020s. Fortune 500 companies made public commitments to their green goals, and whether they met them directly affected CEOs’ year-end bonuses. I thought this might make meaningful progress towards tackling climate risk, but for all the good intentions behind these pay schemes, they failed. Spectacularly so, in fact. ESG targets are regularly hit at a rate of 128%, but we’re still on course to break the seventh of the nine planetary boundaries. So, if we’re overachieving against these targets but our planetary impact is becoming more and more negative, the question has to be asked: where did it all go wrong? It all begins with the targets themselves. In a bid to make them applicable to businesses across industries, they’ve been watered down into a generic checklist, which means a professional services firm and an oil company are often working to the same guidelines despite their environmental impact being vastly different. This generality makes these targets far too easy to hit – it could even be argued that they were designed to be achieved without much effort. One prime example is training completion; if employees sit through a set number of PowerPoints, a business can chalk that target off as a success. If it takes one afternoon to hit an annual ESG target, it’s no wonder we’re careering towards climate disaster. Another reason why ESG-linked executive pay is failing is that the executives it was meant to incentivise haven’t spent much time thinking about hitting these targets. I’m not saying CEOs don’t care about the environment, but when the pay-out for hitting the goals is just 5% of the total bonus pool – and that’s on the high end – it’s not enough to influence decision-making on a scale that delivers tangible change. All of the above is a fatal mixture for sustainability-linked pay in its current state, but there is a solution. We need a new metric, one I’m naming Return on Planet (ROP). The reason I’ve decided to call this new measurable ROP is that it’s built on the same architecture as financial metrics such as Return on Investment (ROI).

body: Mark Segal September 28, 2026 New York City Comptroller Mark Levine announced that he is recommending a strategic expansion in private markets climate solutions investments for three of the City’s public pension funds, with plans to present $5 billion in new private market investment opportunities. New York City’s pension funds represent nearly $300 billion in assets – making them collectively one of the largest public pension systems in the U.S. – and include the New York City Employees’ Retirement System (NYCERS), Teachers’ Retirement System (TRS), and Board of Education Retirement System (BERS). The Comptroller is the investment advisor to and custodian of assets of the city’s pension funds. In 2022, the NYC pension boards launched a Net Zero Implementation Plan, including a target to achieve net zero emissions by 2040, and implementing climate solutions investing as a pillar, with a goal of investing $37.8 billion by 2035. The Comptroller’s office noted that progress on climate solutions investments to date has mostly come from the appreciation of technology stocks in the passive portfolios, and presented private market proactive climate investing strategy as a step toward meeting the pension system’s goal. The new private market opportunities will be focused on areas including renewable power generation, grid modernization, energy efficiency and storage, clean transportation, and building decarbonization, as well as technologies that can reduce pollution, strengthen energy and water security, and improve resilience to extreme weather. Investment opportunities will be presented to each pension board for consideration and approval, subject to each of the three Systems’ independent due-diligence and fiduciary review processes. According to the Comptroller’s office, the new initiative comes as rising energy prices, geopolitical uncertainty, and growing energy demand are putting renewed pressure on energy costs, driving demand for more reliable and resilient energy infrastructure, and presenting attractive investment opportunities for the city’s pension systems.
bodyZh: 马克·西格尔 (Mark Segal) 2026 年 9 月 28 日纽约市审计长马克·莱文 (Mark Levine) 宣布，他建议对纽约市的三个公共养老基金进行私募市场气候解决方案投资的战略扩张，并计划提供 50 亿美元的新私募市场投资机会。纽约市的养老基金代表着近 3000 亿美元的资产，使其成为美国最大的公共养老金系统之一，其中包括纽约市雇员退休系统 (NYCERS)、教师退休系统 (TRS) 和教育委员会退休系统 (BERS)。主计长是该市养老基金的投资顾问和资产托管人。 2022年，纽约市养老金委员会推出了净零实施计划，其中包括到2040年实现净零排放的目标，并以实施气候解决方案投资为支柱，目标是到2035年投资378亿美元。主计长办公室指出，迄今为止，气候解决方案投资的进展主要来自被动投资组合中科技股的升值，并提出了私募市场主动气候投资策略，作为实现养老金制度目标的一步。新的私人市场机会将集中在可再生能源发电、电网现代化、能源效率和存储、清洁交通和建筑脱碳等领域，以及减少污染、加强能源和水安全以及提高抵御极端天气能力的技术。投资机会将提交给每个养老金委员会审议和批准，但须遵守三个系统的独立尽职调查和信托审查流程。据审计长办公室称，这项新举措出台之际，能源价格上涨、地缘政治不确定性和不断增长的能源需求给能源成本带来了新的压力，推动了对更可靠和更有弹性的能源基础设施的需求，并为该市的养老金系统提供了有吸引力的投资机会。

body: Government/ Investors/ Sustainable Finance Mark Segal September 28, 2026 J.P. Morgan Asset Management’s (JPMAM) natural capital unit, J.P. Morgan Natural Capital, and the Office of the President of the Republic of Paraguay announced the launch of a new large-scale sustainable forestry platform, with an investment of approximately $200 million. According to JPMorgan, the new platform investment focuses on establishing commercial forests, advancing native forest restoration, and creating long-term value through the sustainable production of high-quality timber, carbon credits, and wood-products. Capital deployment is expected to begin in early 2027. The partners added that the new initiative is expected to support broader regionalized development, create quality employment in rural areas, and strengthen local communities by combining international capital, Paraguayan capabilities, and the sustainable use of natural resources, with a long-term vision to advance Paraguay’s industrialization by processing timber locally, adding value at the source, and producing finished products for domestic and export markets. Santiago Peña, President of the Republic of Paraguay, said: “This announcement reflects Paraguay’s commitment to creating quality opportunities outside our major cities—building stronger rural communities while stewarding our natural resources responsibly. We welcome long-term partners who invest with a focus on sustainable development, job creation, and adding value in Paraguay.” The new initiative is being developed in partnership with Paraguayan business group Grupo Robinson, which the partners said will contribute local knowledge, production expertise, and a long-term vision for the sustainable development of the sector. The launch of the new platform follows JPMAM’s recent rebranding of its timberland investment advisory company Campbell Global to J.P. Morgan Natural Capital, in a move described by the company as aimed at reflecting the evolution of the business and the growing importance of nature-based assets in institutional portfolios. Angela Davis, CEO of J.P.

body: Environment/ Investors/ Sustainable Finance Mark Segal September 28, 2026 Paris-based international banking and investment group Crédit Agricole announced Monday the launch of Crédit Agricole Capital Naturel, a new division focused on supporting companies, investors and other stakeholders in addressing challenges related to the preservation and restoration of natural resources, with an initial focus on forests. The announcement marks the latest move by major financial players to deepen their focus on the natural capital sector, following JP Morgan’s recently announced rebrand of its timberland investment advisory company Campbell Global to J.P. Morgan Natural Capital, establishing an $11 billion platform positioned to capitalize on broader investment opportunities across land, carbon, biodiversity, and other nature-related investments. According to Crédit Agricole, the new division will bring together expertise from across the firm’s business lines and retail banks to help support clients across Europe across the regeneration value chain by offering them advisory, financing, insurance, investment, project structuring and natural asset enhancement solutions. The bank said that the new division will support companies looking to finance projects, reduce environmental footprint and secure sustainable supplies, investors looking for new asset classes with a sustainable investment objective, owners of natural assets who want to improve the resilience and value of their assets, local authorities committed to preserving their attractiveness, the resilience of their regions and the regeneration of their ecosystems, as well as savers looking to invest in natural capital asset classes and regional banks looking to provide region-specific solutions. As part of the development of the new business line, Crédit Agricole also revealed that it has entered into exclusive negotiations with nature-based solutions developer and operator EcoTree, with a view to acquiring a majority stake in the company.

Morgan Natural Capital)，建立一个 110 亿美元的平台，旨在利用土地、碳、生物多样性和其他自然相关投资领域更广泛的投资机会之后，这一公告标志着主要金融机构加深对自然资本领域关注的最新举措。据法国农业信贷银行称，新部门将汇集该公司各业务线和零售银行的专业知识，通过为欧洲整个再生价值链的客户提供咨询、融资、保险、投资、项目结构和自然资产增值解决方案，为他们提供支持。该银行表示，新部门将支持寻求融资项目、减少环境足迹和确保可持续供应的公司、寻找具有可持续投资目标的新资产类别的投资者、希望提高资产弹性和价值的自然资产所有者、致力于保持吸引力、地区弹性和生态系统再生的地方当局，以及寻求投资自然资本资产类别的储户和寻求提供针对特定地区的解决方案的区域银行。作为新业务线发展的一部分，法国农业信贷银行还透露，已与基于自然的解决方案开发商和运营商EcoTree进行排他性谈判，以期收购该公司的多数股权。

body: Mark Segal September 28, 2026 UK-based banking group Barclays has appointed Paul Williams as its new Global Head of Operational Sustainability. In his new role, Williams will be responsible for leading Barclays’ sustainable operations strategy, embedding sustainability across Procurement, Global Real Estate, Technology and wider business operations to help deliver on the bank’s strategic commitments, regulatory requirements and long-term sustainability objectives. Williams joins Barclays from Deutsche Bank, where he has served since 2024 as Global Head of Sustainable Procurement. Prior to joining Deutsche Bank, he served as Global Head of Environmental & Social Sustainability at international food and beverage group Princes Limited, and he also founded and chairs the Finance Initiative for Sustainable Procurement (FISP), a collaboration of financial services institutions accelerating sustainability performance across shared supply networks.
bodyZh: 马克·西格尔 (Mark Segal) 2026 年 9 月 28 日 英国银行集团巴克莱 (Barclays) 任命保罗·威廉姆斯 (Paul Williams) 为其新任可持续运营全球主管。在他的新职位上，威廉姆斯将负责领导巴克莱银行的可持续运营战略，将可持续发展融入采购、全球房地产、技术和更广泛的业务运营中，以帮助实现该银行的战略承诺、监管要求和长期可持续发展目标。 Williams 从德意志银行加入巴克莱银行，自 2024 年起担任德意志银行可持续采购全球主管。在加入德意志银行之前，他曾担任国际食品和饮料集团 Princes Limited 的环境与社会可持续发展全球主管，他还创立并主持了可持续采购金融倡议 (FISP)，这是一个金融服务机构的合作项目，旨在加速共享供应网络的可持续发展绩效。

body: Mark Segal September 28, 2026 The International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) announced today the launch of ISO/UNDP 53001, Management systems for the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) – Requirements, a new standard aimed at enabling organizations to integrate the UN SDGs into strategy, governance and operations. The UN SDGs refer to the 17 categories of goals adopted in 2015 as part of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, with the aim to protect the planet and improve the quality of life globally. SDG targets include ending poverty and hunger, improving education, and protecting the environment. ISO Secretary-General Sergio Mujica said: “The SDGs have provided a shared global vision for a decade. Today, organizations are looking for concrete ways to translate that vision into action. International Standards have long helped organizations address complex global challenges by providing a common language and a shared framework for action. We are delighted to launch ISO/UNDP 53001 today, extending this proven approach to the SDGs and helping organizations create positive impact for people and planet.” According to ISO and the UNDP, the new standard provides tools to enable organizations to identify and assess their beneficial and adverse impacts, engage relevant interested parties, establish meaningful SDG objectives, collect data and evaluate progress. The new standard specifies requirements for a management system to optimize an organization’s contribution to achieving the SDGs. The standard specifies requirements for analyzing organizational context and engaging with relevant parties to identify, assessing and prioritizing actual and potential impacts, setting organizational SDG objectives and targets, collecting data on impacts, making decisions taking into account the risks that those experiencing the organizations impacts can accept, and understanding and managing interdependencies, synergies and trade-offs to achieve positive results, avoid unintended adverse impacts, and help to achieve the SDGs.
bodyZh: 马克·西格尔 (Mark Segal) 2026 年 9 月 28 日 国际标准化组织 (ISO) 和联合国开发计划署 (UNDP) 今天宣布推出 ISO/UNDP 53001《联合国可持续发展目标 (SDG) 管理体系 – 要求》，这是一项新标准，旨在帮助组织将联合国可持续发展目标纳入战略、治理和运营。联合国可持续发展目标是指2015年通过的17类目标，作为2030年可持续发展议程的一部分，旨在保护地球并提高全球生活质量。可持续发展目标包括消除贫困和饥饿、改善教育和保护环境。 ISO秘书长塞尔吉奥·穆希卡表示：“十年来，可持续发展目标提供了共同的全球愿景。如今，各组织正在寻找将这一愿景转化为行动的具体方法。长期以来，国际标准通过提供共同语言和共享行动框架，帮助各组织应对复杂的全球挑战。我们很高兴今天推出ISO/UNDP 53001，将这一行之有效的方法扩展到可持续发展目标，并帮助各组织为人类和地球创造积极影响。” ISO 和 UNDP 表示，新标准提供了工具，使组织能够识别和评估其有利和不利影响，吸引相关利益方参与，建立有意义的可持续发展目标，收集数据并评估进展情况。新标准规定了管理体系的要求，以优化组织对实现可持续发展目标的贡献。该标准规定了分析组织背景并与相关方合作识别、评估和优先考虑实际和潜在影响的要求，设定组织可持续发展目标的目标和具体目标，收集影响数据，在制定决策时考虑那些遭受组织影响的人可以接受的风险，理解和管理相互依赖性、协同作用和权衡，以取得积极成果，避免意外的不利影响，并帮助实现可持续发展目标。

title: The impact of financing cost differences on global energy and industry decarbonization
summary: Abstract Integrated assessment models usually neglect differences in financing conditions across countries, sectors and time. This omission could distort outcomes concerning electricity generation and also other sectors. Here we estimate and implement dynamic, country-specific cost of capital (CoC) for eight energy and industry sectors in the IMAGE integrated assessment model. Compared with assuming a uniform low-risk CoC, accounting for developing countries’ investment risks increases global mitigation costs through 2100 for staying well below +2 °C by around 9% and shifts cost-effective mitigation efforts to lower-risk regions. Sector-level analysis shows that using granular CoC estimates reduces grid investments in developing countries, shifts centralized heat production towards natural gas and raises green hydrogen costs, slowing electrolysis uptake. In industries such as steel and cement, sector and country risks hinder capital-intensive carbon capture and electricity-based technologies. Our results reveal biases from omitting country-specific financing conditions and highlight the need for climate finance across many sectors.

titleZh: 融资成本差异对全球能源和行业脱碳的影响
summaryZh: 摘要 综合评估模型通常忽略了不同国家、不同行业、不同时间融资条件的差异。这种遗漏可能会扭曲发电和其他部门的结果。在这里，我们在 IMAGE 综合评估模型中估算并实施了八个能源和工业部门的动态、特定国家的资本成本 (CoC)。与假设统一的低风险CoC相比，考虑到发展中国家的投资风险，到2100年，全球保持远低于+2°C的缓解成本将增加约9%，并将具有成本效益的缓解努力转移到风险较低的地区。行业层面的分析表明，使用精细的 CoC 估算可以减少发展中国家的电网投资，将集中供热生产转向天然气，并提高绿色氢成本，从而减缓电解的采用。在钢铁和水泥等行业，部门和国家风险阻碍了资本密集型碳捕获和电力技术。我们的结果揭示了由于忽略特定国家融资条件而产生的偏差，并强调了许多部门对气候融资的需求。

title: Sustainability reporting frameworks and environmental disclosure coverage in the Indian infrastructure industry: an empirical comparison of GRI and BRSR
summary: As the infrastructure industry affects the environment in many aspects, it ought to be evaluated and addressed through standardized reporting frameworks that create transparency and accountability for entities’ stakeholders. To comprehend the significance of these frameworks for communicating entities’ sustainable performance, it becomes necessary to examine various frameworks used and their level of acceptance in the infrastructure industry. Using prominent sustainability reporting frameworks such as the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) and Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR), this study examined the level of acceptance and alignment through in-depth content analysis, with specific reference to environmental disclosures. Additionally, the study used the Environmental Disclosure Index standard metric to assess the extent of environmental disclosures by companies in their non-financial reporting for the financial year (FY) 2024-2025, using a sample of five infrastructure industry companies. The findings demonstrate significant convergence between the BRSR and GRI frameworks in their environmental disclosure standards, yet each framework also contains indicators specific to its unique regulations and institutional context. Case companies exhibited similar and acceptable environmental disclosure quality (EDCI ranging from 0.49–0.71), while BRSR coverage varied notably, indicating the framework’s capacity to allow for voluntary indicator reporting. Notably, while BRSR addresses many environmental impacts crucial to the infrastructure industry, other aspects, such as noise pollution and construction-related disturbances, remain outside of its current disclosure scope. This study contributes to the BRSR-based sustainability disclosure literature by taking a sector-specific approach, providing policymakers and academics with insights for aligning national and international reporting requirements in emerging economic contexts.

titleZh: 印度基础设施行业的可持续发展报告框架和环境信息披露覆盖范围：GRI 和 BRSR 的实证比较
summaryZh: 由于基础设施行业在许多方面影响环境，因此应该通过标准化报告框架对其进行评估和解决，从而为实体的利益相关者创造透明度和问责制。为了理解这些框架对于沟通实体可持续绩效的重要性，有必要检查所使用的各种框架及其在基础设施行业中的接受程度。本研究利用全球报告倡议组织 (GRI) 和企业责任与可持续发展报告 (BRSR) 等著名的可持续发展报告框架，通过深入的内容分析（特别是环境披露）来检验接受程度和一致性。此外，该研究还使用环境披露指数标准指标来评估公司在 2024-2025 财年 (FY) 非财务报告中的环境披露程度，并以五家基础设施行业公司为样本。研究结果表明，BRSR 和 GRI 框架在环境披露标准方面存在显着趋同，但每个框架还包含针对其独特法规和制度背景的指标。案例公司表现出相似且可接受的环境披露质量（EDCI 范围为 0.49-0.71），而 BRSR 覆盖范围差异显着，表明该框架允许自愿指标报告的能力。值得注意的是，虽然 BRSR 解决了许多对基础设施行业至关重要的环境影响，但其他方面，例如噪音污染和与建筑相关的干扰，仍然超出了其当前的披露范围。

title: Listening to the mountain: oral history, biocultural heritage, and sustainability transitions in Serra da Estrela
summary: This article draws on a corpus of oral history interviews collected in Serra da Estrela, Portugal, to examine how community memory, territorial knowledge, and lived relationships with the mountain contribute to understanding socio-ecological change and rethinking sustainability in a context of climate disruption. Focusing on territory already recognized as a UNESCO Global Geopark and currently proposed for inscription as a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, the study explores how oral testimony illuminates the biocultural dimensions of sustainability and the contribution of the Social Sciences and Humanities to sustainability transitions. The research adopts a qualitative, interpretive, and place-based design grounded in the Memory for All methodology and combines documentary analysis with oral history interviews addressing everyday life, pastoral activity, environmental perception, territorial change, and intergenerational transmission of knowledge. The results show that the interviews consistently converge around a set of major themes: the decline of pastoralism, demographic contraction, changing climatic conditions, wildfires, institutional inadequacy, and the reconfiguration of local economies. They also reveal Serra da Estrela as a lived socio-ecological system in which ecological processes, labor, memory, and identity remain deeply entangled. Particular attention is given to transhumance, analyzed through both historical literature and interview-based testimony as a practice that links mobility, adaptation, ecological knowledge, and cultural memory, while also acquiring renewed relevance in contemporary debates on biodiversity, fuel-load management, and regenerative territorial practices. The article argues that oral history enlarges the epistemic field of sustainability research by making audible forms of knowledge and experiences that remain only partially translated into technical and policy-oriented approaches. In doing so, it shows how methods grounded in the Social Sciences and Humanities can help reframe sustainability transitions as processes of cultural and epistemic transformation and contribute to more inclusive, territorially grounded, and socially meaningful pathways toward sustainable and circular societies. The findings also provide practical insights for policymakers, protected-area managers, and local stakeholders seeking to integrate community knowledge and biocultural heritage into sustainability transitions.

body: Every country tells itself a story about who it is. For most of the past hundred years, Australia’s story was simple and comfortable: It was the lucky country, where with a bit of effort, great results came naturally. “She’ll be right, mate,” as the uniquely Australian idiom puts it. Now, that story has changed, replaced by the very different sense that progress is stalling, that the country is no longer doing well, and that the birthright of prosperity is slipping away. Only 22 percent of Australians believe the next generation will be better off.12026 Edelman Trust Barometer: Trust amid insularity: Australia report, Edelman Trust Institute, 2026. Their lived experience suggests why: The country has not had such a slow decade of income growth since before the Second World War.2Jutta Bolt and Jan Luiten van Zanden, Maddison Project Database 2023 (adjusted for purchasing-power parity so that income levels can be compared across countries); Global Economic Model, Oxford Economics, 2025; GDP per capita (constant LCU), series NY.GDP.PCAP.KN, World Bank Group, July 2026 edition. Data from the World Bank uses each country’s own constant local currency. The Maddison Project and the World Bank show the same profile albeit different growth rates. But the story and the current perception share a flaw. Each casts Australia as a passive recipient of fortune: lucky then, unlucky now. Australia’s true experience is very different: It has made its own luck through deliberate choices, actions, and plain old “hard yakka.” That is the lesson offered in particular by Australia’s two boom periods (1945 to 1970 and 1993 to 2015)—periods we can learn from. The McKinsey Global Institute (MGI), in its book A Century of Plenty, offers a global perspective with additional lessons.3A Century of Plenty: A Story of Progress for Generations to Come, McKinsey Global Institute, 2026. MGI’s research demonstrates that the past century brought material advances in standards of living globally, and that a second century of plenty is within reach. The same is true for Australia.

title: From Project Outputs to Governance Capacity: A Multi-Scale Reflective Case Study of SDG-Oriented Peri-Urban Rural Regeneration in Hsinchu City, Taiwan
summary: Peri-urban rural regeneration is often assessed through completed projects or administrative indicators, while the governance mechanisms that sustain rural sustainability receive less attention. This article examines how project-based participation can be translated into governance capacity in Hsinchu City, northwestern Taiwan. Adopting an evidence-bound reflective documentary case-study design, it analyzes policy, spatial planning, training, community project, and rural regeneration records from the 2025 Hsinchu City Community Rural Regeneration Guidance Program. The findings show that regeneration operates through municipal coordination, functional clusters, community participation, and site-based interventions. Six intermediate capacities are identified: proposal-making, coordination, maintenance, interpretive, sustainability-translation, and resilience capacities. The study contributes a transferable framework linking rural sustainability, SDG localization, ESG-oriented governance, and peri-urban regeneration through explicit evidence-use boundaries. It does not claim verified long-term impacts on income, carbon reduction, biodiversity, demographic change, or resident satisfaction; rather, it clarifies how governance capacity may be generated and where future independent verification is required.

summaryZh: 城郊乡村复兴往往通过已完成的项目或行政指标进行评估，而维持乡村可持续性的治理机制却很少受到关注。本文探讨了如何将基于项目的参与转化为台湾西北部新竹市的治理能力。采用有据可依的反思性文献案例研究设计，分析了2025年新竹市社区乡村更新指导计划的政策、空间规划、培训、社区项目和乡村更新记录。研究结果表明，重建通过市政协调、功能集群、社区参与和基于场地的干预措施来运作。确定了六种中间能力：提案制定、协调、维护、解释、可持续性翻译和复原能力。该研究通过明确的证据使用边界，提供了一个可转移的框架，将农村可持续发展、可持续发展目标本地化、以 ESG 为导向的治理和城郊复兴联系起来。

title: Corporate governance drivers of ESG disclosure in Saudi non-financial listed firms
summary: Abstract Corporate governance (CG) serves as a critical internal determinant of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosure transparency, yet empirical evidence from emerging Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) markets remains underdeveloped. This study investigates the impact of key corporate governance attributes on ESG disclosure practices within the Saudi Arabian non-financial firms. Utilizing an unbalanced panel dataset of 171 firm-year observations from 100 non-financial firms listed on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul) over the period 2020–2024, the study employs content analysis to operationalize ESG disclosure through two complementary measures: a GRI-aligned binary index (ESGD1) and the natural logarithm of ESG-related word counts (ESGD). To address potential endogeneity, unobserved heterogeneity, and dynamic persistence, the empirical baseline established via fixed-effects panel regression with cluster-robust standard errors is rigorously supplemented by two-stage least squares (2SLS) estimation and a dynamic System Generalized Method of Moments (System-GMM) framework. The empirical findings reveal that board gender diversity, CEO power, executive compensation, the presence of a dedicated sustainability committee, and overall firm size exert a positive and highly significant influence on both the volume and quality of ESG disclosures. Conversely, board size and financial leverage exhibit a significant negative relationship with ESG reporting, while board independence, ownership structure, and financial profitability (ROA) demonstrate no statistically significant direct impact. These insights suggest that rather than general board oversight, targeted governance structures specifically specialized sustainability committees, enhanced executive gender diversity, and strategic executive incentive alignment are the primary internal criteria driving corporate sustainability transparency. The results offer critical policy and managerial implications for the optimization of governance frameworks under the transformation mandates of Saudi Vision 2030 and evolving Tadawul disclosure guidelines.

titleZh: 沙特非金融上市公司 ESG 披露的公司治理驱动因素
summaryZh: 摘要 公司治理 (CG) 是环境、社会和治理 (ESG) 披露透明度的关键内部决定因素，但来自新兴海湾合作委员会 (GCC) 市场的经验证据仍然不发达。本研究调查了沙特阿拉伯非金融公司的关键公司治理属性对 ESG 披露实践的影响。该研究利用了 2020 年至 2024 年期间沙特交易所 (Tadawul) 上市的 100 家非金融公司的 171 家公司年度观察的不平衡面板数据集，采用内容分析，通过两种补充措施来实施 ESG 披露：GRI 对齐的二进制索引 (ESGD1) 和 ESG 相关字数的自然对数 (ESGD)。为了解决潜在的内生性、未观察到的异质性和动态持久性，通过具有集群稳健标准误差的固定效应面板回归建立的经验基线由两阶段最小二乘法 (2SLS) 估计和动态系统广义矩法 (System-GMM) 框架严格补充。

title: Artificial Intelligence and Corporate Sustainability Disclosure: Evidence from Corporate Climate Risk Disclosure in China
summary: As artificial intelligence becomes more deeply embedded in corporate sustainability governance, it remains unclear whether public policies centered on AI development are linked to changes in corporate sustainability disclosure. Focusing on corporate climate risk disclosure as an important dimension of sustainability disclosure, this study examines how China’s National Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Development Pilot Zone policy, referred to as the AI Pilot Zone policy, is associated with firms’ disclosure of climate-related risks. Using Chinese A-share listed firms from 2014 to 2023 and a multi-period difference-in-differences approach, we find that the AI Pilot Zone policy is associated with higher levels of corporate climate risk disclosure. A series of robustness checks further confirms the stability of this finding. Mechanism analysis provides suggestive evidence consistent with three channels: climate-related information-processing capability, climate risk governance capability, and external monitoring pressure. The subsample estimates reveal that the association is more pronounced among firms under greater environmental pressure, firms with higher levels of institutional ownership, and firms whose managers exhibit stronger green awareness. Additional analysis suggests that climate risk disclosure is positively associated with ESG performance, especially environmental and governance performance. This study contributes firm-level empirical evidence on the association between AI-oriented public policies and corporate climate risk disclosure, while highlighting the need to distinguish disclosure improvement from substantive sustainability transformation.

title: Between law and market: voluntary ESG disclosure as a legal counterpoint to mandatory governance in China
summary: This article analyzes voluntary Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) disclosure as a complementary governance tool in Chinese listed companies from a legal analysis perspective. While most countries initially favored mandatory ESG disclosure, recent regulatory adjustments in Europe and the U.S. have revealed significant drawbacks, including rigidity, high compliance costs, and inconsistent disclosure. In China, these limitations are further complicated by a layered regulatory structure, uneven firm capacity, and the coexistence of administrative guidance, exchange self-regulation, and market-based ESG evaluation. Using soft-law governance as the dominant analytical framework, and drawing on institutional complementarity, signaling theory, the efficient market hypothesis, and policy compliance willingness as supporting mechanisms, this study argues that voluntary ESG disclosure can operate above a mandatory legal baseline. It can provide more tailored, firm-specific, and forward-looking information, improve transparency, and reduce information asymmetry for investors when supported by credible verification, reputational discipline, and market-based rewards. The article also cautions that voluntary disclosure may generate selective disclosure, symbolic compliance, and greenwashing if it is not supported by baseline mandatory rules, credible third-party assurance, and clear liability boundaries. Current voluntary disclosure in China faces challenges, including weak enforcement, vague guidance, insufficient safe-harbor protections, misaligned incentives, free-rider problems, and barriers specific to SMEs. To address these problems, the article recommends improving regulatory clarity, strengthening market-based incentives, developing effective third-party assurance, expanding safe-harbor protections, and investing in ESG capacity building.

title: Mandate or Market? Climate-Disclosure Regulation and the Quality of Corporate Climate Governance: Evidence from Staggered Adoption Across Four Economies
summary: Climate-related disclosure has moved rapidly from a voluntary practice to a legal obligation, yet whether mandates improve the substance of corporate climate governance—rather than the volume of reporting—remains an open question. We exploit the staggered introduction of climate-disclosure mandates in the United Kingdom (2022) and France (2025), with the United States and Australia serving as never-treated and not-yet-treated comparison groups, to estimate the effect of mandatory disclosure on structured climate-governance quality. The outcome is the Transition Pathway Initiative (TPI) Management Quality score, an externally assessed 0–5 staircase of climate-governance practices, observed for 837 listed firms over 2015–2025 (2841 firm-year observations). Using two-way fixed effects, Sun–Abraham and Callaway–Sant’Anna estimators implemented in RStudio, we find no statistically significant effect of disclosure mandates on climate-governance quality: the preferred Callaway–Sant’Anna estimate is 0.082 levels (95% CI −0.221 to 0.385), precise enough to rule out effects larger than about 0.4 levels (≈0.4 standard deviations). Meanwhile, never-mandated US firms improved from a mean Management Quality of 1.4 to 3.1 over the decade, converging toward mandated jurisdictions. An anticipation-adjusted specification yields a positive and significant effect, but it benchmarks against pandemic-year assessments and should be read with caution. Disaggregating the score into its underlying indicators shows that board-level oversight and basic disclosure are near-universal among mandated firms, whereas transition-planning and capital-alignment practices remain rare in every jurisdiction, locating the unfinished governance agenda at the top of the staircase. The evidence suggests that disclosure mandates largely codified governance practices that investor- and market-driven pressures had already diffused, implying that regulators should pair disclosure requirements with substantive transition-plan obligations if the policy goal is governance change rather than transparency alone.

title: LLM-Assisted and Rule-Based Assessment of ESG Disclosure Quality and Its Association with External ESG Ratings: Exploratory Evidence from S&P 500 Energy Firms
summary: Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosure has become an important source of information for external stakeholders. As sustainability reporting has expanded, distinguishing disclosure quantity from disclosure quality has become increasingly important. This study examines how sustainability disclosure quality is associated with external ESG evaluation outcomes among Standard & Poor’s (S&P) 500 Energy Sector firms. ESG-related claims were identified and classified from sustainability reports using large language model (LLM)-assisted structured content analysis. Based on the resulting corpus, three disclosure quality indicators were constructed: the Quantitative Evidence Ratio (QER), the Target Accountability Ratio (TAR), and the Reporting Infrastructure Score (RIS). These indicators were integrated into a composite Disclosure Quality Index (DQI) and examined in relation to S&P Global ESG Scores using Spearman’s rank correlation. The results indicated limited positive associations for the individual indicators, whereas the composite DQI showed a more pronounced positive relationship. Disclosure–rating divergence patterns were also observed, indicating that relatively favorable disclosure quality positions do not consistently correspond to higher ESG Score rankings. Overall, the findings suggested that sustainability disclosure quality may be multidimensional and that its association with external ESG evaluation outcomes became more apparent when disclosure characteristics were considered in combination. However, because the analysis is restricted to a small sample of S&P 500 Energy Sector firms, the findings should be interpreted as exploratory sector-specific evidence with limited generalizability.

title: ESG Rating Disagreement as a Greenwashing Signal: Asymmetric Effects of Digital Transformation Through Disclosure and Performance Channels
summary: This study examines whether ESG rating disagreement is a leading indicator of corporate greenwashing and how digital transformation (DTI) moderates this relationship through disclosure and performance channels. Using 8111 firm-year observations from Chinese A-share companies (2012–2022), we employ two-way fixed-effects panel regression complemented by Bayesian-optimised machine learning models interpreted through SHAP. Aggregate rating disagreement is a strong and robust predictor of greenwashing. Channel decomposition reveals asymmetric DTI moderation: the disclosure channel amplifies greenwashing risk as digitally advanced firms expand reporting capacity to widen the gap between disclosed and actual ESG performance (bloom_DTI: β = +0.2471, p < 0.01), while the performance channel attenuates greenwashing risk as digital operational monitoring translates substantive performance into a measurable reduction (hua_DTI: β = −0.2804, p < 0.01). This pattern is robust across ownership structure, pollution intensity, and region. Machine learning analysis confirms the econometric findings and reveals nonlinear threshold effects invisible to panel regression. This asymmetric channel mechanism contributes to the ESG rating divergence literature and has implications for disclosure regulation and ESG-based investment screening.

summaryZh: 本研究探讨了 ESG 评级分歧是否是企业洗绿的先行指标，以及数字化转型 (DTI) 如何通过披露和绩效渠道调节这种关系。利用中国 A 股公司的 8111 家公司年度观察（2012-2022 年），我们采用双向固定效应面板回归，并辅以通过 SHAP 解释的贝叶斯优化机器学习模型。总体评级分歧是洗绿的有力预测因素。渠道分解揭示了不对称的 DTI 调节：随着数字化先进企业扩大报告能力，扩大披露与实际 ESG 绩效之间的差距，披露渠道放大了洗绿风险 (bloom_DTI: β = +0.2471, p < 0.01)，而绩效渠道则减弱了洗绿风险，因为数字化运营监控将实质性绩效转化为可测量的减少 (hua_DTI: β = -0.2804, p < 0.01) 0.01）。这种模式在所有制结构、污染强度和地区范围内都很有效。机器学习分析证实了计量经济学的发现，并揭示了面板回归看不见的非线性阈值效应。
